exposure: dietary intakes (niacin, sodium, vitamin B6, fat)
outcome: gut microbiota functions (carbohydrate and lipid metabolism)
cohort: The study included 22 obese and 24 normal-weight Korean children aged 5-13.
finding: Obese Korean children aged 5-13 showed a lower relative abundance of the phylum Bacteroidetes and altered gut microbiota composition and functions related to carbohydrate and lipid metabolism compared to normal-weight children.
